faces.south-west (Willem de Zwijgerlaan, stree: evidence: ref-sw.jpg. White render, 6 + 9 window pairs per floor on a 3.64 m pitch, Corten atrium at t 20.8-26.2, Corten plinth with shopfront glazing, two stone bands, cornice.
faces.north-east (canal): evidence: ref-ne.jpg from the water. Two Corten floors with window pairs on a 5.05 m pitch, terrace with glass balustrade, white setback storey with ribbon windows, five-column pergola. Vertical scale taken from the first-floor window row (the quay fender hides the base). Corten windows beyond the photographed 43 m (t < -10 and > 33) repeat the pitch (inferred).
faces.north-west and south-east ends: INFERRED: hidden behind a brick shop (SE) and a warehouse (NW) up to ~7 m; only the upper two floors show over them. Modelled on the south-west pair rhythm; ground floors left as 3DBAG blank wall behind the neighbours.

caveats: NE roofline: the real white storey stops at ~13 m and the pergola beam (15.6 m) floats on columns over open air. 3DBAG fills this with solid wall to 15.2-15.6 m, kept as is (an attempt to rebuild it opened mesh holes because the single 3DBAG roof lid cannot be cut). Pergola columns and beam are drawn on the NE plane.
Corten wall and white storey windows on the NE face are drawn on the 3DBAG plane; the true setback is 2 m.
